result.title: IsoAct: Geometry-Aware Post-hoc Debiasing via Isometric Actions
result.summary: Learning representations that are robust to nuisance factors is essential for reliable deployment, but remains challenging when the representations lie on non-Euclidean manifolds. Existing debiasing methods typically assume Euclidean representations or apply linear interventions, which can distort the geometry of structured latent spaces. We propose IsoAct, a post-hoc framework that accounts for geometry in both nuisance identification and representation editing. It identifies nuisance-predictive directions using Fisher discriminant analysis (FDA) in tangent coordinates and applies corrections through manifold-native actions that preserve manifold membership. Controlled and real-world experiments on hyperspherical, hyperbolic, and $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ representations evaluate nuisance reduction, utility preservation, and manifold validity jointly. IsoAct reduces nuisance recoverability while retaining competitive utility. Its clearest joint result is on KLIFS, combining reduced kinase-group recoverability, strong structural prediction, and valid rigid poses.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 IsoAct 后处理去偏框架：在切空间用 Fisher 判别分析定位 nuisance 预测方向，再以保持流形归属的等距作用编辑表示；在超球、双曲与 SE(3) 表示上联合评估去偏效果、效用保持与流形有效性。
